title: DAG simulation of a sequential circuit
statement: Let a Boolean sequential circuit have $n$ input bits, $r$ registers, a combinational DAG on its inputs and register contents, a next value for each register, and an initial register state. For every integer $T\ge 1$, there is a DAG circuit on the same $n$ inputs whose output agrees with the sequential circuit's output after $T$ steps, and whose size is at most $2((r+g)T+n)$, where $g$ is the number of gates in the combinational DAG. If the combinational DAG is well formed, so is the resulting DAG; if it is well formed and every gate has at most two arguments, then the resulting DAG has those same properties.
hypotheses_covered: A sequential circuit with $n$ inputs and $r$ registers
The combinational circuit is a DAG on $n+r$ sources
At least one step is run: $1\le T$
For the well-formedness conclusion: the combinational circuit is well formed
For the fan-in-two conclusion: the combinational circuit is well formed and each gate has at most two arguments
